one_line: Sanskrit poet‑scholar of Vallabhi whose Bhattikavya wove Ramayana epic, grammar and poetics into one ingenious mahakavya.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, lean and slightly bookish build with calm, focused posture
appearance.face: oval face, medium wheatish complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, thoughtful almond-shaped eyes, default expression a gentle, observant half-smile as if weighing words in his mind
appearance.hair: dark brown-black hair, straight and pulled back into a small, low knot at the nape; a simple narrow cream-coloured cloth headband tied around the forehead, with its ends tucked neatly above the ears
appearance.costume: a scholar’s version of a 7th‑century western Indian dhoti and uttariya: lower garment is a finely pleated cotton dhoti in soft matte ivory tied at the waist and falling to the ankles; upper body covered with a long-sleeved, thigh-length kurta-style tunic in muted warm beige with a very subtle woven border at cuffs and hem in dark maroon; over this, a light cotton uttariya (shawl) in pale saffron draped from left shoulder across the chest and around the back, creating layered folds; he wears simple brown leather sandals, a thin maroon waist sash knotted slightly to the left, and minimal jewellery—a single small gold stud in one ear and a plain narrow copper bangle on his right wrist; no royal insignia, but clothing is clean, orderly and slightly refined to show his standing at Vallabhi’s scholarly court.
appearance.signature: a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a dark maroon cord held in his left hand, with a simple wooden stylus tucked into the cord, symbolising the Bhattikavya as a crafted teaching epic

ref_desc: Bhatti is a lean mid-30s scholar with an oval wheatish face, short beard, low-knotted dark hair and cream headband, wearing an ivory dhoti, beige tunic, pale saffron shawl, maroon sash and simple sandals, holding a maroon-tied palm-leaf manuscript and stylus in warm ivory, saffron and maroon tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Bhatti: a lean Sanskrit poet-scholar in his mid-30s with an oval wheatish face, thoughtful almond eyes, straight nose and neatly trimmed short beard and moustache. His dark brown-black hair is straight, pulled into a small low knot at the nape, with a narrow cream headband tied across his forehead and tucked over the ears. He wears an era-accurate 7th-century Vallabhi scholar’s outfit: a finely pleated ivory cotton dhoti tied at the waist and falling to the ankles; a long-sleeved, thigh-length warm beige tunic with very subtle dark maroon woven borders at the cuffs and hem; and a pale saffron cotton shawl (uttariya) draped from his left shoulder across the chest and around the back, creating soft, layered folds. A thin dark maroon waist sash is knotted slightly to his left, and his feet are in simple brown leather sandals. Jewellery is minimal—a single small gold stud in one ear and a narrow copper bangle on his right wrist—to show modest refinement, not royalty. In his left hand he carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a dark maroon cord, with a plain wooden stylus tucked into the cord, his signature prop symbolising the Bhattikavya and its hidden grammatical teachings. Use a harmonious palette of ivory, warm beige, pale saffron, dark maroon and brown, and present him front, back and a close-up of the head to clearly show his consistent face, hair, garments, and manuscript prop.
